name: dp::thread_pool (DeveloperPaul123/thread-pool)
workload: 256x256 matrix multiplication run through each pool, timed with nanobench, relative to dp::thread_pool with std::function.
claimed_speedup: Own table (MSVC): dp::thread_pool std::function 93.27 ms/op (100%), with std::move_only_function 90.66 ms/op (102.9%), BS::thread_pool 99.73 ms/op (93.5%), task_thread_pool 91.29 ms/op (102.2%), riften::Thiefpool 93.18 ms/op (100.1%). README says it is 'faster than other thread pool libraries in most cases' but notes riften pulls ahead in some cases and task_thread_pool wins with many small tasks.
compiler_and_flags: MSVC for the quoted table; flags not stated
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5800X (16 x 3800 MHz), 32 GB RAM
tradeoffs: Simple shared-queue pool with per-thread queues and work stealing; C++20; needs std::move_only_function for best speed. Not a fork-join or task-graph scheduler.
caveats: Margins against BS::thread_pool are about 7 percent, other pools are within noise or ahead; one workload only; compares against other small thread pools, not TBB, OpenMP or Rayon; compiler flags not stated for the quoted table.
found_via: WebSearch 'faster than OpenMP lightweight C++ parallel_for thread pool library github benchmark'; opened README via raw.githubusercontent.com

name: poolSTL
baseline: std::execution::par (native C++17 parallel algorithms; backing runtime not stated)
workload: Google Benchmark of parallel STL algorithms (all_of, find_if, for_each, sort, transform, exclusive_scan, reduce) on large arrays, poolstl::par versus std::execution::par and sequential.
claimed_speedup: Mixed. exclusive_scan: poolstl::par 11.6 ms vs std::execution::par 19.8 ms vs sequential 33.7 ms. sort: poolstl::par 112 ms vs std par 113 ms vs sequential 603 ms; pluggable_sort with pdqsort 71.7 ms. for_each: poolstl 18.7 ms vs std par 15.3 ms (slower). reduce: 4.06 ms vs 3.38 ms (slower).
hardware: Apple M1 Pro (6 performance + 2 efficiency cores)
tradeoffs: Header-only thread-pool backend for C++17 parallel algorithms for compilers without native support; random-access iterators only, no nested parallel calls.
caveats: Mostly parity or slower than native std::execution::par; wins only in exclusive_scan and when a pluggable sort is swapped in; single machine; which standard library and parallel backend implement std::execution::par on that machine is not stated; own results.
found_via: WebSearch result alugowski/task-thread-pool README pointing at poolSTL; opened README via raw.githubusercontent.com
